newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Long Australian bonds shrug off shorts' woes.
newsitem.headline: Long Australian bonds shrug off shorts' woes.

text.p: *Long-dated Australian bonds shrugged off the woes of the short-end to finish firm, building on Tuesday's post-tender rally, although trade was light ahead of the U.S. bond auction.
*January labour force data due on Thursday.
Long-dated Australian shrugged off the initial woes of the short-end to finish firm, building on Tuesday's post-tender rally, although trade was light ahead of the U.S. bond auction later today.
"The long-end looks in great shape. Even if we follow down any gyrations in the U.S., I think you will find good support 10 basis points from here (on futures)," one trader said.

Comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane on Tuesday were seen by the long-end as remaining hawkish on inflation, but for the short-end they put another dent in hopes of a further monetary policy easing.
Macfarlane said the impact of previous rate cuts were feeding through and the economy appeared to be showing improvement, making it logical for the bank to wait for further developments on wages.

His reference to wages was seen pointing to the current 8.75 percent "living wage" proposal by the trade union movement. The RBA has already warned of marked acceleration in wages growth if this was fully implemented.
March bill futures fell sharply in after hours trading and never reallly during the day as the market re-adjusted to the unchanged policy stance.

The March bill contract fell to 94.07, indicating a cash bill rate only just below current 6.0 percent official interest rates and having now dropped some 25 basis points since last week's strong quarterly wages data.

While Macfarlane was more upbeat on the economy, consumers were less happy with Westpac's February consumer sentiment index falling 7.9 percent, bringing the index to its lowest level since September last year.
Although Macfarlane has put the focus squarely back on wages growth, Thursday's labour force report for January will be heavily scrutinized, analysts added.

The local yield curve flattened with the short-end under pressure. The long-end of market slightly outperformed the U.S. ahead of the second leg of the U.S. refunding which sees US$12.0 billion of 10-year notes up for sale. Canadian debt also faces a 10-year C$2.3 billion bond auction later today.

March bill futures broke down through anticipated support at 94.11 in SYCOM, but found a base at 94.07, which has proved supportive on two previous occasions since the official interest rate cut to 6.0 percent on December 11.
